Briefly stated, the case of the prosecution is that on 15.02.2022 at about 02:15 PM at Platform No.
1, Laxmi Nagar Metro Station, within the jurisdiction of YDM, both accused attempted to cheat the complainant Azad Khan for a sum of Rs. 50,000/- after having induced him by showing three packets of currency notes of Rs. 500/- each (1.5 lakh), whereas each of the packet was having only one original currency note of Rs. 500/- on both sides of the packets and rest were waste papers.

Accused persons were apprehended by the complainant at the spot red handed alongwith the said fake trio packets of currency notes which they were found retaining dishonestly, fraudulently and deceitfully.
Further, accused persons induced the complainant to deliver/transfer Rs. 50,000/-.
Investigation was carried out accordingly.
2. Upon completion of investigation charge sheet was filed and both the accused were summoned.
Pursuant to appearance of the accused persons, they were supplied with the copy of charge sheet in compliance of Section 207 Cr.P.C.
Thereafter, the matter was listed for consideration on charge.

3. Upon hearing the arguments advanced by the Ld. Counsel for the accused persons and on perusal of record, prima facie case for offence punishable u/s 420/511/34 IPC were found to be made out against accused persons.
Accordingly, charge was framed against the accused persons to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Matter was then fixed for prosecution evidence.

Thereafter, due to non-apperance of accused Najim Sekh, he was CR Cases 1794/2022 Page no. 2 of 7 State Vs. Sahil PS Yamuna Bank Metro Digitally signed by DEEKSHA DEEKSHA RAO RAO Date:

They noticed that three boys were sitting on bench at Platform No. 1 and were talking to each other.
One out of trio namely Azad Khan told him that the boys who were sitting with him had attempted to cheat him for Rs. 50,000/-.
The names of those boys who were present with the complainant were Sahil and Nazim Sekh.

LEGAL PRINCIPLES INVOLVED 9.

In order to substantiate the allegations, prosecution was required to prove beyond reasonable doubts following facts to prove that the accused has committed offence u/s 420/511/34 IPC:
i.

The accused must have cheated and thereby dishonestly induced the complainant to deliver any property, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is capable of being converted into a valuable security and, ii. the accused must have attempted to commit the offence and in such attempt must have done some act towards the commission of the offence.
10. Presumption of innocence is a cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence.
The burden of proving guilt of the accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.

In Partap vs. State of U.P., (1976) 2 SCC 798,
the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the burden on the accused is not as onerous as that which State vs Sahil on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175437285/
3 lies on the prosecution and that the prosecution is required to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt, whereas, the accused can discharge his onus by establishing a mere preponderance of probability.

APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE 11.

In the present case, accused Sahil alongwith co-accused Nazim Sekh (since PO) allegedly,
dishoneslty, fraudulenty and decietfuly induced the complainant Azad Khan to deliver a sum of Rs.
50,000/- after showing him three packets of currency notes of Rs. 500/- each which actually contained only one original currency note of Rs. 500/- on both sides of the packets and the rest were waste papers.
PW/complainant Azad Khan against whom the alleged offence was committed, could not be examined as he was not traceable despite repeated efforts and was dropped from the list of witnesses.
Nothing incriminating could come in the testimony of PW1 so as to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
The other witnesses were mere formal witnesses and hence their examination was dispensed with.
12. In view of the above facts, it is quite clear that no evidence has come on the record against the accused as the complainant could not be examined.
No other evidence or material witness was examined/mentioned by the prosecution to establish its case against the accused.
13. It is trite that non availability of a victim or complainant to be examined can never be ground to acquit accused if there is evidence otherwise available proving criminal act of accused.

However, as discussed herein above, there is no such evidence to prove the criminal act of accused and considering the CR Cases 1794/2022 Page no. 6 of 7 State Vs. Sahil PS Yamuna Bank Metro Digitally signed by DEEKSHA DEEKSHA RAO RAO Date:
2025.06.04 16:06:11 +0530 overall facts of the case, version of the prosecution cannot be stated to be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
CONCLUSION 14.

In order to substantiate the allegations, prosecution was required to prove beyond reasonable doubts following facts to prove that the accused has committed offence u/s 420/511/34 IPC:
i.
The accused must have cheated and thereby dishonestly induced the complainant to deliver any property, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is capable of being converted into a valuable security and, ii. the accused must have attempted to commit the offence and in such attempt must have done some act towards the commission of the offence.
10. Presumption of innocence is a cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence.
The burden of proving guilt of the accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.
In order to establish the guilt of the accused, each and every element of the offence has to be proved beyond reasonable doubt by leading reliable, independent and unimpeachable evidence, unless otherwise provided by the statute.
PW/complainant Azad Khan against whom the alleged offence was committed, could not be examined as he was not traceable despite repeated efforts and was dropped from the list of witnesses.
Nothing incriminating could come in the testimony of PW1 so as to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
The other witnesses were mere formal witnesses and hence their examination was dispensed with.
12. In view of the above facts, it is quite clear that no evidence has come on the record against the accused as the complainant could not be examined.
13. It is trite that non availability of a victim or complainant to be examined can never be ground to acquit accused if there is evidence otherwise available proving criminal act of accused.
However, as discussed herein above, there is no such evidence to prove the criminal act of accused and considering the CR Cases 1794/2022 Page no. 6 of 7 State Vs. Sahil PS Yamuna Bank Metro Digitally signed by DEEKSHA DEEKSHA RAO RAO Date:
2025.06.04 16:06:11 +0530 overall facts of the case, version of the prosecution cannot be stated to be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
CONCLUSION 14.
In a criminal trial, onus is on the prosecution to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
It is the duty of prosecution to travel the entire distance from may have to must have and in case the story of prosecution lacks credibility or appears to be doubtful, the benefit of doubt must go in favour of the accused.
In view of the discussion made herein above and considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, this court is of the view that the prosecution has completely failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
